raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

An async KV-connector load is admitted only if it fits in the free pool minus one spec decode step (#57104, per KV cache group since #59880). Near `max_model_len` that margin can exceed what the request can still use, so a load that fits the pool is never admitted and every request behind it waits. This PR caps each group's margin at the blocks left before `max_model_len`.

## Claims

- Each group's margin is capped at the blocks between the request's computed prefix and `max_model_len`. It is never larger than before, and it changes only for a request within one spec step of `max_model_len`.
- In the reproducer below, the stalled request is admitted, loads its remote KV and completes, and an unrelated request on the same server completes.

## Validation

The new test fails on main for the reported reason and passes with this PR:

```console
$ pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py::test_async_load_margin_capped_at_max_model_len
# main (f81a414fa)
E       assert <RequestStatus.WAITING: 1> == <RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS: 3>
1 failed
# this PR, whole file
17 passed
```

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`, `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` and `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 3,248 passed with this PR and 3,247 on main. Both trees have the same 19 failures and 2 collection errors, which need offline-unavailable model downloads, `ray` or a Mooncake bootstrap service, or fail identically on main.

End to end on an RTX A6000 (Qwen3-0.6B with dummy weights, eager, `--max-model-len 240 --block-size 16 --num-gpu-blocks-override 16`, so 15 usable blocks, and n-gram speculation with 16 tokens). Two `vllm serve` processes use the CPU plus P2P `TieringOffloadingSpec`. The consumer receives a 231-token request with a 224-token remote hit (14 blocks), then an unrelated request with a 5 s timeout:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remote-hit request | stays `WAITING` | 200 in 0.11 s |
| Unrelated request | timed out | 200 in 0.04 s |
| `/health` | 200 | 200 |

DFlash with 8 speculative tokens gives the same result. N-gram with 8 tokens does not stall, because its spec step fits in one block. With 17 GPU blocks, main completes both requests, which confirms that the stall comes from the admission margin.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
serve() {  # serve HTTP_PORT P2P_PORT
  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port "$1" --served-model-name m --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
    --seed 0 --generation-config vllm --max-model-len 240 --max-num-seqs 2 --max-num-batched-tokens 128 \
    --num-gpu-blocks-override 16 --block-size 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.38 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":16,"prompt_lookup_max":4,"prompt_lookup_min":2}' \
    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":67108864,"offload_prompt_only":false,"block_size":16,"secondary_tiers":[{"type":"p2p","host":"127.0.0.1","port":'"$2"',"backends":["UCX"],"num_threads":2,"unbound_store_timeout_s":20.0}]}}'
}
serve 8100 34120 &  # source
serve 8200 34121 &  # consumer
```

```python
import threading, time, requests

def post(port, prompt, max_tokens, params=None, timeout=None):
    body = {"model": "m", "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0, "seed": 0}
    if params:
        body["kv_transfer_params"] = params
    return requests.post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/completions", json=body, timeout=timeout)

prompt = "Tenant marker capacity-impact. Preserve this private context." + " context" * 220  # 231 tokens
post(8100, prompt, 1, {"remote_decoder": {"kv_request_id": "r1"}})
hit = {"remote_prefiller": {"kv_request_id": "r1", "remote_host": "127.0.0.1", "remote_port": 34120}}
threading.Thread(target=post, args=(8200, prompt, 24, hit), daemon=True).start()
time.sleep(2)
print(post(8200, "An unrelated request." + " context" * 30, 24, timeout=5))  # main: ReadTimeout
```

</details>

## Details

Root cause: admission reserves `_spec_decode_step_blocks`, a constant number of blocks per group for one spec decode step. Slots never extend past `max_model_len`, so a request within one step of the limit can use fewer blocks than that. When the load plus the full margin exceeds the whole pool, `allocate_slots` fails even with every block free, and the `break` in the waiting loop holds the queue behind the request.

The margin from #57104 and #59880 keeps its purpose. It is only reduced where the request cannot use the blocks, and startup already guarantees that one `max_model_len` sequence fits, so a lone request can always be promoted. Replacing the `break` with a skip would also unblock later requests, but it changes FCFS admission and leaves the impossible request stuck, so this PR does not do it. The scheduler change adds 21 lines and no GPU work.

CI: the test module is marked `cpu_test` and runs in the "(CPU) V1 Others" step. The end-to-end case needs two servers with a P2P tier, which no CI step provides, so it was validated locally as above.

Duplicate-work check: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for async load admission, waiting-queue head-of-line blocking and spec reservations. #45406 and #58442 (both closed, unmerged) address other async-load stalls. #64379 (open) speeds up async admission without changing its decisions. It rewrites the same `reserved_blocks` expression, so whichever lands second only needs `self._spec_decode_step_blocks` replaced by `self._spec_decode_step_margin(num_computed_tokens)`. I found no matching report or fix.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to investigate, implement, test and draft this PR.

+def test_async_load_margin_capped_at_max_model_len():
+    """An async load that fits the pool is admitted even when a full spec
+    decode step would reach past max_model_len."""
+    block_size = 16
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_model_len=block_size * 15,
+        num_speculative_tokens=16,
+    )
+    # create_vllm_config sets only the scheduler's limit.
+    vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len = block_size * 15
+    # 15 usable blocks. The load needs 14, a spec step would reserve 2 more,
+    # but the request can only grow by 1 before max_model_len.
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config, num_blocks=16)
+    request = create_request(
+        request_id=1,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_tokens=block_size * 14 + 8,
+        do_remote_prefill=True,
+        max_tokens=8,
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    with patch.object(
+        scheduler.connector,
+        "get_num_new_matched_tokens",
+        return_value=(block_size * 14, True),
+    ):
+        scheduler.schedule()
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
+
+    # The load lands: the request is promoted and scheduled.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        scheduler.schedule(),
+        create_model_runner_output([], finished_recving={request.request_id}),
+    )
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING
+    assert scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id] > 0
+
